text.p: Argentina placed 250 million pesos in 91-day treasury bills (Letes) at a cut-off yield of 7.60 percent and another $250 million in 182-day Letes at 6.80 percent, the Economy Ministry said Tuesday.
The price at the cut-off yield of 7.60 percent on the 91-day bills was 980.789. There were 74 bids for a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.06 times.
The price at the cut-off yield of 6.80 percent on the 182-day bills was 965.622. There were 87 bids for a bid-to-cover ratio of 5.23 times.

Of the 250 million pesos of 91-day bills sold, 21 million pesos were allocated on non-competitive bids, while of the $250 million 182-day bills placed, $20.5 million were allocated on non-competitive bids.
At last months' auction of 91-day peso bills there was a cut-off yield of 7.21 percent. The last time 182-day dollar bills were issued was in August, when there was a cut-off yield of 6.49 percent.
Market-makers will be offered up to 10 percent more of both issues until 1730 local/2030 GMT Tuesday.
